# SAFe Program Increment Planning Template

**Agile Release Train:** [ART Name]  
**Program Increment:** [PI Number]

**Location:** [Physical Location and/or Virtual Meeting Details]  
**Facilitator:** [Name]  
**Last Updated:** [YYYY-MM-DD]

## 📋 PI Planning Overview

Program Increment (PI) Planning is a cadence-based, face-to-face event that serves as the heartbeat of the Agile Release Train (ART), aligning all teams to a shared mission and vision. This two-day event brings together all ART members to:

- Align on a common mission and vision
- Identify dependencies and foster cross-team collaboration
- Commit to PI objectives with business value
- Address risks and impediments
- Create team and program plans for the upcoming PI

## 🔄 PI Planning Preparation Checklist

### 2-4 Weeks Before

- [ ] Confirm PI Planning dates and location
- [ ] Reserve venue with adequate breakout spaces
- [ ] Prepare virtual meeting setup if needed
- [ ] Send calendar invitations to all participants
- [ ] Engage with Product Management on vision and priorities
- [ ] Begin preparing feature backlog

### 1-2 Weeks Before

- [ ] Finalize and prioritize Program Backlog
- [ ] Refine Features to INVEST criteria
- [ ] Prepare Business Context presentation
- [ ] Finalize Architecture Vision presentation
- [ ] Create/update Planning Board for dependency tracking
- [ ] Prepare Team Breakout rooms/areas
- [ ] Ensure teams have completed pre-PI Planning backlog refinement
- [ ] Distribute agenda to all participants

### 1-3 Days Before

- [ ] Confirm logistics (room setup, catering, technology)
- [ ] Print physical materials (if applicable)
- [ ] Test all technology platforms
- [ ] Final review of Feature readiness
- [ ] Prepare Risk and Impediment tracking mechanisms
- [ ] Brief facilitators and Scrum Masters on responsibilities

## 📅 PI Planning Agenda

### Day 1

| Time | Activity | Lead | Description |
|------|----------|------|-------------|
| 08:30 - 09:00 | Check-in and Setup | All | Arrival, setup, and networking |
| 09:00 - 09:15 | Welcome and Logistics | RTE | Welcome, agenda review, logistics |
| 09:15 - 09:45 | Business Context | Business Owners | Market trends, business direction, competitive analysis |
| 09:45 - 10:30 | Product/Solution Vision | Product Management | Vision, roadmap, top 10 features |
| 10:30 - 11:00 | Architecture Vision | System Architect | Technical direction, standards, NFRs |
| 11:00 - 11:15 | Planning Context & Guardrails | RTE | Planning process, expectations, constraints |
| 11:15 - 12:00 | Team Breakouts - 1 | Teams | Initial planning, story breakdown |
| 12:00 - 13:00 | Lunch | All | |
| 13:00 - 15:30 | Team Breakouts - 2 | Teams | Continue planning, draft objectives |
| 15:30 - 16:30 | Draft Plan Review | Team Reps | Present draft plans, identify dependencies |
| 16:30 - 17:00 | Management Review | Leadership | Review progress, address blockers |
| 17:00 - 17:30 | Problem-Solving Workshop | As needed | Address major issues identified |

### Day 2

| Time | Activity | Lead | Description |
|------|----------|------|-------------|
| 08:30 - 09:00 | Check-in | All | Day 1 recap, adjustments to plans |
| 09:00 - 11:30 | Team Breakouts - 3 | Teams | Finalize plans, address dependencies |
| 11:30 - 12:30 | Final Plan Review | Team Reps | Present final plans, updated objectives |
| 12:30 - 13:30 | Lunch | All | |
| 13:30 - 14:30 | Program Risks | RTE | Review and address program risks |
| 14:30 - 15:00 | Confidence Vote | All | Teams vote on confidence in the plan |
| 15:00 - 16:00 | Plan Rework (if needed) | Teams | Address concerns from confidence vote |
| 16:00 - 16:30 | Planning Retrospective | All | What went well, what to improve |
| 16:30 - 17:00 | Closing | RTE/Leaders | Final words, next steps, celebration |

## ⚠️ Program Risks and Impediments

### ROAM Board

| ID | Risk/Impediment | Type | Probability | Impact | ROAM Status | Owner | Mitigation Plan |
|----|-----------------|------|-------------|--------|-------------|-------|-----------------|
| R-1 | [Example] Third-party API integration may be delayed | External Dependency | Medium | High | Owned | Integration Lead | Early engagement with vendor, develop fallback plan |
| R-2 | [Example] Team capacity reduced due to planned vacations | Resource | High | Medium | Accepted | Scrum Masters | Adjust capacity planning, identify backup resources |
| R-3 | [Example] New technology stack has learning curve | Technical | Medium | Medium | Mitigated | Architects | Schedule training sessions in first iteration |
| R-4 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-5 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-6 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-7 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-8 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-9 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| R-10 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

**ROAM Legend:**
- **Resolved:** The risk has been addressed and no longer exists
- **Owned:** Someone has taken responsibility for resolving the risk
- **Accepted:** The risk cannot be resolved, but the organization accepts it
- **Mitigated:** Action has been taken to reduce the probability or impact

2. Low confidence - Might work with significant adjustments
3. Moderate confidence - Should work with minor adjustments
4. High confidence - Will work as planned with minimal risk
5. Very high confidence - Will definitely work as planned

## When to Use

Use throughout the project lifecycle to identify, assess, and track risks. This template is essential for projects with significant complexity, multiple stakeholders, or high business impact, where structured risk management provides decision-making value.

## When NOT to Use

Do not use for very low-risk, short-duration tasks where informal risk awareness is sufficient. Avoid this template if your governance framework requires a different risk management approach or if stakeholders prefer real-time risk dashboards over static registers.

## Appendix A: Role Definitions

- **RTE (Release Train Engineer):** Facilitates the ART process and events, escalates impediments
- **Product Management:** Defines features and participates in planning to provide clarification
- **System Architect/Engineering:** Establishes technical direction and assists teams during planning
- **Business Owners:** Participate in planning, approve plans, and assign business value
- **Scrum Master:** Facilitates team planning, helps coordinate with other teams
- **Product Owner:** Works with teams to define stories and acceptance criteria
- **Development Team:** Defines user stories, estimates, identifies risks and dependencies

## Appendix B: PI Planning Success Factors

1. **Face-to-face participation** (or high-quality virtual experience)
2. **Proper preparation** (features ready, capacity planning done)
3. **Right participants** (all team members, leadership, stakeholders)
4. **Focus on business outcomes** (not just features)
5. **Real-time decision-making** (business owners present)
6. **Commitment-based planning** (not assignment)
7. **Continuous adjustments** during planning
8. **Fast feedback** on plan quality (confidence vote)
